Counterpoint Research has published a new report showing that Apple overtook Samsung in Q2 2026 to become the largest smartphone brand in Europe's carrier channel, as telecom sales proved more resilient than the overall market. Details below.

Apple drives carrier sales to outperform Europe's overall smartphone market

According to a report published today by Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales through carriers in Europe fell 4% year-on-year in Q2 2026, compared with an 11% decline in the open market. The report shows overall smartphone sales dropped 8%.

Counterpoint says this once again shows the impact of rising memory costs, which has hit the European low-end smartphone market particularly hard. Meanwhile, carrier sales have been more resilient because the channel tends to favour premium devices and premium brands such as Apple, with more consumers purchasing handsets through contracts.

The report notes that Apple's share of smartphone sales through European carriers rose from 33% in Q2 2025 to 37% in Q2 2026; over the same period, Samsung's share fell from 39% to 34%.

Elsewhere, Chinese brand vivo posted the largest year-on-year increase in carrier sales, at 90%; Motorola trailed far behind in second place with 27% growth.

Below is Counterpoint Research Associate Director Jan Stryjak's response to the figures:

Stryjak added that the carrier channel is expected to continue gaining share "over the coming quarters" as "the low end will continue to be impacted by the memory crisis." He also noted that independent retailers have stepped up promotions compared with carriers, "which may ease some of the price pressure and provide additional stimulus to the open market."
